items.title: The formal completion of an affine scheme along a closed subset, and its types
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: For an affine scheme X with a closed subset T, the lemma asserts three things about the formal completion of X along T: that it is adic* when the complement of T is quasi-compact, that it is the formal spectrum of the adic completion with respect to a finitely generated ideal cutting out T, and that it is Noetherian when X is (statement lines 3275-3287). The proof reduces the first two assertions to the second: if either the complement is quasi-compact or the scheme is Noetherian, then T is cut out by a finitely generated ideal, and in the Noetherian case the adic completion of a Noetherian ring is Noetherian, so it suffices to identify the completion in the case of an ideal cut out by finitely many elements (proof lines 3289-3296). That identification is a direct computation: a morphism from an affine scheme into X whose image lies in T has each of the chosen generators nilpotent after pullback, so some power of the ideal maps to zero, which says exactly that the functor is the filtered colimit of the spectra of the quotients by the powers of the ideal, that is the formal spectrum of the adic completion (proof lines 3298-3306). The claim is H2: the reduction of the two other assertions to the second uses the finite generation criterion in one case and permanence of Noetherianness under completion in the other, and the explicit identification of the functor is carried out.
